description: When a newly detected face has several look-alikes, when is it attached to an existing person right away, when is a new person created, and when is the decision postponed? Why can two such decisions running at once not corrupt each other?
anchor_note: non-bug task: root_cause_symbols holds the anchor (entry point / changed symbol); RC metrics are reported for category A only

source.verification: Read the 'handleRecognizeFaces' tests in server/src/services/person.service.spec.ts (describe at line 1300; individual test names not enumerated by me - UNVERIFIED). Independent evidence of the lock location: commit 477452b5c diff.
source.notes: The lock is a Postgres advisory lock shared across processes (needed for multi-replica deployments), not a queue concurrency setting.

notes: Logic verified entirely in PersonService.handleRecognizeFaces (person.service.ts:562-651): attach if match has a personGroupId (core or deferred), create group+person only when isCore, else defer once via JobRepository.queue deferred:true (:603-607), serialised by DatabaseRepository.withLock (database.repository.ts:461-475: in-process AsyncLock + postgres advisory lock).
Anchor/root should be handleRecognizeFaces, not handleDetectFaces (the latter only queues FacialRecognition via queueAll, :451-452, not JobRepository.queue).
handleQueueRecognizeFaces (person.service.ts:501-505) also takes the same DatabaseLock.FacialRecognition lock - relevant to "why not corrupt", so it is a weak distractor.
